subject: Catalyst: request for uptime tolerance & service credit amendment
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@catalyst.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Kathy Lin <kathy.lin@catalyst.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T16:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA details and final push

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — one more ask from our side before procurement signs off. For our regulated telehealth customers we need the following in the contract: an uptime target of 99.99% (monthly), and a cap on aggregate service credits at 25% of monthly fees (we understand standard is higher but we need an explicit cap). We also want a tighter 95th-percentile latency SLO for the inference endpoint at 150ms for the main model (the smaller models can be 250ms).

I realize this is outside standard terms — happy to attach a redline. Procurement is working on a PO but wants to confirm these items by 12/18 to meet Q4 close. Can you advise whether Redwood can accept the uptime tolerance and the explicit credit cap, and if any pricing or term changes will be required?

Appreciate it,
Samir
Director, Platform Partnerships
Catalyst Systems

--
Attachment: Catalyst_SLA_Amendment_v3.pdf (proposed redline)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-08T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Catalyst SLA request — need exec signoff

Ben / Grace — forwarding Samir's ask. Quick summary: Catalyst (strategic, high ACV) is requesting nonstandard SLOs: uptime 99.99% and an explicit service credit cap at 25%, plus a latency 95p at 150ms for their main model. They want confirmation by 12/18.

Impact / considerations:
- Commercial: they are asking for a contract-level cap on credits (reduces our downside). They also expect a 20% new-customer discount tied to multi-region deployment (part of negotiation).
- Operational: 95p@150ms is aggressive for cross-region traffic; we can offer that on dedicated instances or if they accept pinned model + reserved capacity.
- Legal: needs a short indemnity/monitoring clause and rollback option if latency regression occurs during rollout.

Attachments: Catalyst_SLA_Amendment_v3.pdf, Catalyst_ServiceCredits_Table.xlsx (pricing impact table).

Ask: Can you sign off on an exception that: 1) permits 99.99 uptime with a 25% credit cap, 2) requires they commit to Dedicated or Dedicated-equivalent capacity (we'll attach a T&M engineering credit for initial tuning), and 3) approves a 15% commercial concession instead of 20% if we take the lower 25% cap? If you approve, I will send the updated SLA to Samir and request DocuSign.

Time-sensitive: procurement target 12/18.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Catalyst SLA request — need exec signoff

Marissa — thanks for the summary. I support approving the uptime exception and explicit 25% cap, provided we attach two things: (a) a one-time engineering onboarding credit (up to 40 hours) to tune latency and (b) a clause that limits the cap to the first 12 months of the contract (reverts to standard terms afterward).

Commercial concession: I prefer 15% discount concession in exchange for the credit cap and dedicated capacity requirement. Legal to confirm on precise indemnities, but this looks reasonable from a commercial standpoint.

Ben

Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-12-10T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Approval: Catalyst SLA exception (conditional)

Marissa / Ben — after reviewing the ask and the commercial tradeoffs I authorize the following exception for Catalyst Systems, conditional on Legal and Engineering sign-off: 

1) Approve uptime target 99.99% with an explicit aggregate service credit cap of 25% for months 1-12.
2) Approve latency SLO of 95p@150ms only if Catalyst commits to Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) and we include a 60-day tuning and verification period before the SLA becomes effective.
3) Reduce the commercial concession to 15% (vs. 20% requested) in exchange for the credit cap + dedicated commitment.
4) Require an automatic reversion clause at month 13 to standard SLA terms unless both parties agree in writing to extend.
5) Require monitoring hooks (tracing + 95p telemetry) and an engineering-led runbook; the one-time engineering credit (40 hours) is approved.

Next steps: Marissa, please route the redline to Legal for final language on indemnities and the rollback clause. Once Legal signs off, prepare DocuSign using the linked template: https://redwood.app/docusign/CAT-042. I will be copied on the final signature request.

Grace Occonnor
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Samir Desai <samir@catalyst.ai>, Kathy Lin <kathy.lin@catalyst.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-10T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA details and final push — approval & next steps

Samir / Kathy — good news: Redwood can accept the requested uptime tolerance and an explicit service credit cap with the following agreed items (condensed):

- Uptime: 99.99% (monthly). Aggregate service credit cap of 25% of monthly fees for months 1–12.
- Latency: 95th-percentile SLO of 150ms for the main model, conditionally approved if Catalyst signs for Dedicated capacity and we complete a 60-day tuning/verification window.
- Commercial: Redwood will provide a 15% new-customer concession (reduced from your 20% ask) in exchange for the credit cap and dedicated capacity commitment.
- Onboarding: Redwood will include a one-time engineering onboarding credit (up to 40 hours) to aid latency tuning.
- Governance: SLA will include monitoring hooks and an automatic reversion to standard SLA terms at month 13 if no mutual extension is executed.

Attached: Catalyst_SLA_Amendment_v3.pdf (updated redline reflecting the conditional approvals) and Catalyst_ServiceCredits_Table.xlsx (commercial impact). Please review and confirm. If this looks good I will send the DocuSign packet (https://redwood.app/docusign/CAT-042) and loop Legal for final language.

We aim to have signatures prior to 2026-12-18 to hit your procurement timeline — let me know if you need anything faster.

Best,
Marissa Cole
